newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot near value ceiling - CentreInvest.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot near value ceiling - CentreInvest.

text.p: Russian international air carrier Aeroflot is closing in on its fair valuation, Moscow-based brokerage CentreInvest Securities said in a recent report.
Research chief James Fenkner said the company's unlisted shares traded at $122 on Tuesday, close to a risk-adjusted target of $134.

Aeroflot-Russian International Airlines traded between $20 and $35 for most of 1996, but the sharp rise this year has given it a price-earnings ratio of 19 -- comparable to leading Russian companies such as oil producer LUKoil.
"It has a P/E similar to LUKoil without the reserves," Fenkner said.
CentreInvest said modernisation and traffic increase on international and domestic routes, especially after the Russian economy began to grow, would strengthen Aeroflot's profits.

It should be able to attract funds with an American Depositary Receipt to allow foreign share trading in September, and state control could allow it to attract up to $1.5 billion in five-year, government-guaranteed loans.
A stable exchange rate would help the international carrier, which has been hurt by the rouble's depreciation against the dollar. Passenger loads, now below industry average, could also increase.
The best case scenario would see 1997 profit more than double on a year ago and the P/E ratio fall to about six, CentreInvest said.
